title: Overcoming Feelings of Intimidation
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece frames intimidation as purely a function of perception, arguing that people can only feel intimidated when they grant a perceived imbalance the power to shape their self-view. It describes the counterproductive behaviors intimidation tends to trigger, becoming tongue-tied, overly deferential, or completely frozen, and how the visible awkwardness often worsens the underlying anxiety. Alongside standard advice about self-talk and avoiding comparison, the piece offers a more unusual recommendation: using mild, self-deprecating humor about the situation to diffuse its power and regain a sense of agency.
points: Intimidation is described as purely a function of perception, requiring the person to grant it power.
Common counterproductive reactions include becoming tongue-tied, overly deferential, or completely frozen.
Standard advice includes reminding yourself of past strengths and avoiding direct comparison to others.
A more unusual recommendation: using mild self-deprecating humor to diffuse the situation's power.
quotes: The feeling of being intimidated is uncomfortable at best, and terrifying at worst.
It's important to recognize that intimidation is solely a function of perception and belief.
You can’t be intimidated by anyone or anything unless you give the perceived differences the power to influence the view you have of yourself.
A more unusual approach is to find humor in the situation or person.
The most important idea is to never accept feelings of intimidation.
